newsitem.title: USA: US Comptroller urges banks to help flood victims.
newsitem.headline: US Comptroller urges banks to help flood victims.

text.p: A top U.S. bank regulator gave financial institutions a green light to ease up on borrowers badly hurt by recent floods and ice storms in the western and midwestern portions of the country.
Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said banks should help victims of recent natural disasters by extending the terms of loans or restructuring borrowings.
"The OCC recognizes that the effects of natural disasters on local individuals and businesses are often temporary," Ludwig said in an official bulletin released Monday.
"Prudent efforts to adjust or alter terms on existing loans in affected areas affected by the floods and related problems should not be subject to examiner criticism," Ludwig said.

The Comptroller's office supervises about 2,800 nationally chartered U.S. banks. Absent the comptroller's bulletin, examiners charged with ensuring the safety and soundness of banks might question easing of loan terms by banks in affected areas.
Ludwig said banks could also ease credit-extension terms for new loans to certain borrowers, consistent with prudent banking and risk management practices.
"This will help such borrowers recover their financial strength and place them in a better position to service their debts," Ludwig said.
The Comptroller's office will also accelerate its approval process for banks with destroyed or damaged branches seeking to set up temporary facilities.
